incidents.summary: Lloyds Banking Group settled with the US government for $350 million over transactions that circumvented US restrictions by concealing the source of funds.

sources.title: Lloyds Banking Group
sources.quote: They did this by stripping information out of wire transfers, thereby concealing the source of funds.

sources.title: Lloyds Banking Group
sources.quote: Lloyds Banking Group settled with the US government for US$350 million.

incidents.summary: Lloyds and Bank of Scotland face two lawsuits connected to Arena Television's collapse, alleging inadequate scrutiny of suspicious transactions.

sources.title: What the £1.2 billion Arena TV fraud case means for FI and D&O insurers | Insurance Business
sources.quote: Liquidators allege the bank processed years of suspicious transactions without asking enough questions - questions that, had they been asked, might have unravelled the fraud far sooner.

sources.title: What the £1.2 billion Arena TV fraud case means for FI and D&O insurers | Insurance Business
sources.quote: One, brought against both Lloyds and Bank of Scotland by Arena's own liquidators, seeks around £280 million.

sources.title: What the £1.2 billion Arena TV fraud case means for FI and D&O insurers | Insurance Business
sources.quote: A second and much larger claim, brought by Sentinel's administrators against Lloyds alone, is seeking the return of more than £1 billion.

incidents.summary: Lloyds received a £160,000 sanctions penalty after Halifax opened an account for a designated person and processed payments before freezing the account.

sources.title: Lloyds fined for breaching Russian sanctions after opening an account for an ally of Putin | This is Money
sources.quote: The High Street lender was hit with a penalty of £160,000 after its Halifax arm allowed Dmitry Ovsyannikov to become a customer in 2023 – even though he was a ‘designated person’.

sources.title: Lloyds fined for breaching Russian sanctions after opening an account for an ally of Putin | This is Money
sources.quote: Ovsyannikov, whose father was born in Bradford, opened the Halifax account on February 6, 2023, and the bank processed 24 payments totalling £77,383 between February 8 and February 24.

sources.title: Lloyds fined for breaching Russian sanctions after opening an account for an ally of Putin | This is Money
sources.quote: But a fuller review did identify him as a designated person, and the account was frozen and the authorities were informed.

incidents.summary: A 2025 report states that historical payment protection insurance mis-selling cost Lloyds £22 billion.

sources.title: Lloyds mulls legal action over £11bn car finance scandal payout proposals | This is Money
sources.quote: The scandal has been dubbed ‘PPI on wheels’ as it echoes mis-sold payment protection insurance which cost Lloyds £22billion over a decade ago.

incidents.summary: Lloyds faces motor-finance mis-selling litigation involving 30,000 customers and has said it will not challenge the UK's compensation scheme.

sources.title: Lloyds bank faces £66m court battle with car loan customers | Lloyds Banking Group | The Guardian
sources.quote: Lloyds Banking Group is facing a court battle with 30,000 aggrieved car loan customers who are to abandon the City regulator’s official redress scheme amid fears it will shortchange consumers and favour lenders.

sources.title: Lloyds mulls legal action over £11bn car finance scandal payout proposals | This is Money
sources.quote: Britain’s biggest lender has set aside almost £2billion to cover potential payouts to millions of drivers who bought cars on finance with hidden commission payments between 2007 and 2024.

sources.title: Lloyds Banking Group
sources.quote: In April 2026, the Financial Times published that Lloyds will not launch a legal challenge against the UK's compensation scheme to consumers who were mis-sold the car finance agreements.

incidents.summary: The information watchdog questioned Lloyds over a potential privacy breach involving access to 30,000 staff bank accounts during pay talks, and Lloyds subsequently began investigating.

sources.title: Lloyds questioned by watchdog over use of staff banking data in pay talks | Lloyds Banking Group | The Guardian
sources.quote: The information watchdog is questioning Lloyds Banking Group over a potential breach of privacy rules after it accessed data from 30,000 staff bank accounts during union pay talks last year.

sources.title: Lloyds investigating after using staff’s bank account data in pay talks | Lloyds Banking Group | The Guardian
sources.quote: Lloyds investigating after using staff’s bank account data in pay talks
